<!--
Shared partial: the opening of every lecture's notes.

Included directly after the front matter of each notes.qmd. The wording is
identical everywhere on purpose. A module may give its first lecture a longer
version instead, which also says WHY the written material is in English;
students then meet that explanation once, and this short form after it.

ONE FIXED EXAMPLE, not one per lecture (Martin, 2026-09-25). The per-lecture
example term would need a value in every notes file, and a missing or misspelled
one prints a placeholder that no check catches. A consequence to remember: the
example here is NOT the German gloss of any lecture's own terms. Each notes file
must gloss its key terms at their first use in the body, as the style guide asks.
-->

These notes are the complete written version of the session. The slides are
shorter. Everything that is said in the lecture but not shown on a slide is
written out here.

::: {.callout-note title="Language"}
The written material is in English. The lecture, the practical and the
**exam** are in German. The notes give each key term with its German equivalent
in parentheses when the term first appears, for example: sequencing (dt.
*Sequenzierung*). Many German terms in this field are the same as the English
ones, and the notes say so where this is the case.
:::
